stories.title: VIC Partners Obtains Construction Loan for 268-Unit FW Workforce Rental Community
stories.excerpt: VIC Partners obtained a $36.5 million primary line of credit for the construction of Vic Centre, a 268-unit workforce-housing development at 7120 Anderson Blvd. in Fort Worth outside of Loop 820 and north of Interstate 30. The project is being developed by Vic Partners and M-13 Construction. OakNorth Bank will provide the loan as part of a $48 million joint financing with Hickory CRE Capital, a commercial real estate lender. Concord Summit Capital arranged the construction loan. VIC suggests the cost of the construction will be $41.7 million. The development will consist of nine three-story residential buildings, a clubhouse, fitness center, pickleball court and business center along with 402 parking spaces.  The post VIC Partners Obtains Construction Loan for 268-Unit FW Workforce Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: VIC Partners closes $48M construction financing (OakNorth + Hickory CRE) for 268-unit workforce rental in Fort Worth
Vic Centre at 7120 Anderson Blvd; $41.7M total development cost; nine 3-story buildings north of I-30
Workforce housing focus signals continued demand for affordable multifamily outside Loop 820 corridor
stories.summary: VIC Partners and M-13 Construction obtained a $48 million joint construction loan from OakNorth Bank and Hickory CRE Capital (arranged by Concord Summit Capital) for Vic Centre, a 268-unit workforce-housing community on Anderson Boulevard in Fort Worth north of I-30. Total development cost is $41.7 million. The project includes nine three-story residential buildings, amenities (clubhouse, fitness center, pickleball court, business center), and 402 parking spaces.
stories.impact: Workforce housing at moderately elevated rents remains financeable and attractive to institutional lenders in Fort Worth's suburban rings, where land and labor costs support value-add underwriting. This signals sustained demand for B/B+ product outside prime corridors as workforce migration to DFW continues to outpace high-amenity core supply absorption.

stories.title: W Properties Mixing BTR and Garden-Style Apartments in Melissa
stories.excerpt: W Properties plans to build a 252-unit garden-style multifamily community on approximately 12 acres adjacent to Everbloom (shown), the company’s 343-unit build-to-rent community in Melissa, Texas. The company said it’s taking a different approach with garden-style apartments, a sector still working through elevated supply and concessions across North Texas. Texas multifamily permitting across its five major metros has fallen by more than half from its 2023 peak, while Dallas-Fort Worth continues to absorb a significant pipeline of apartments already under construction. W Properties Andrew Welker added, “BTR and garden-style apartments are different products, and we would not have started a garden-style project in that same environment. We expect to go vertical by mid-2027, positioning this community for an early 2029 leasing season, when we believe today’s supply pressure will look materially different.” The post W Properties Mixing BTR and Garden-Style Apartments in Melissa appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: W Properties begins garden-style 252-unit project adjacent to 343-unit BTR community in Melissa, Texas
DFW multifamily permitting down >50% from 2023 peak; developer deliberately delays leasing to early 2029
Acknowledges current elevated supply/concessions in North Texas; expects material market reset by project delivery
stories.summary: W Properties is planning a 252-unit garden-style multifamily community on approximately 12 acres in Melissa, Texas, adjacent to its existing 343-unit build-to-rent (BTR) community Everbloom. The developer explicitly stated it would not have started the garden-style project in the current environment and is timing vertical construction for mid-2027 to position the community for a leasing season in early 2029, betting that supply pressures will have materially diminished by then. Texas multifamily permitting has fallen more than 50% from its 2023 peak.
stories.impact: DFW's supply correction is real but incomplete: even aggressive, well-capitalized developers are explicitly timing delivery 2–3 years out to avoid today's concession environment. This signals that despite declining permits, near-term absorption will remain challenged in Dallas-Fort Worth. Underwriting windows for garden-style (vs. BTR) will remain compressed through 2027–28 unless significant job growth or population migration accelerates demand.

stories.title: REITs Post Record High FFO in Q2 2026: Nareit
stories.excerpt: REITs posted record highs for funds from operations (FFO) and net operating income (NOI) in 2026’s second quarter while maintaining strong balance sheets, according to Nareit’s latest REIT Industry Tracker. More than 70% of REITs reported year-over-year increases in FFO, while nearly 80% reported year-over-year increases in NOI. Industry Tracker data show that FFO reached $22.4 billion in Q2, up 12.4% Y-O-Y. Meanwhile, NOI reached $32.7 billion, up 6.8%. Additionally, same-store NOI experienced a 4.1% Y-O-Y gain, demonstrating that REIT operations outpaced inflation in the second quarter, which was 3.5% “The strength we’re seeing from the REIT industry isn’t coming from one measure or sector,” said John Worth, EVP of research & investor outreach at Nareit. “Across the board, REITs continue to generate strong income from their properties reflecting rising occupancy while maintaining robust balance sheets. That combination speaks to the underlying resilience of the industry amid ongoing economic uncertainty.” The post REITs Post Record High FFO in Q2 2026: Nareit appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: REITs posted Q2 2026 FFO of $22.4B (+12.4% Y-O-Y); NOI reached $32.7B (+6.8% Y-O-Y)
>70% of REITs increased FFO Y-O-Y; ~80% increased NOI; same-store NOI +4.1% Y-O-Y vs. 3.5% inflation
Strong occupancy and balance sheets driving sector resilience despite broader economic uncertainty
stories.summary: The REIT industry posted record highs for funds from operations and net operating income in Q2 2026. FFO reached $22.4 billion, up 12.4% year-over-year, while NOI hit $32.7 billion, up 6.8%. More than 70% of REITs reported Y-O-Y FFO growth and nearly 80% reported Y-O-Y NOI growth. Same-store NOI grew 4.1% Y-O-Y, outpacing inflation (3.5%), driven by rising occupancy and robust balance sheets.
stories.impact: Strong REIT earnings and balance sheets support continued capital availability for multifamily development and acquisition, but the 4.1% same-store NOI growth suggests sector-wide rent growth is moderating toward single digits. This limits return expectations for new development unless located in high-demand submarkets with structural supply constraints or strong in-migration tailwinds.

stories.title: Downtown Phoenix Luxury Hotel to Debut September 16
stories.excerpt: Pacific Hospitality Group (PHG) is taking reservations for its latest hotel, the Denu Hotel & Spa in downtown Phoenix. The 236-room hotel is at 1 E. Adams Street in downtown Phoenix in a newly constructed 17-story building. Features include the Hammam-inspired spa, the Solstone Holistic Spa offers thermal rituals and immersive treatments; a fitness and wellbeing program; a rooftop pool with sweeping city views; and versatile meeting and event spaces designed to accommodate everything from corporate gatherings to celebratory social occasions. Denū is located steps from major transportation hubs, the convention center and the city’s arts, culture, sports and entertainment venues. A lobby-level restaurant and lounge, café and rooftop bar complete the experience. PHG operates both branded and independent resort properties. The company manages, develops, finances, and owns hotels and resorts in California, Hawaii, Arizona and Texas. PHG currently owns and manages 11 hotels and resorts, representing over 2,463 rooms and 185,791 square feet of indoor meeting and event space. The post Downtown Phoenix Luxury Hotel to Debut September 16 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pacific Hospitality Group opens 236-room Denū Hotel & Spa in downtown Phoenix (September 16, 2026)
17-story building at 1 E. Adams Street; spa, rooftop pool, meeting space, restaurant/lounge/café/bar
Hospitality rebound in Phoenix core; likely signals confidence in convention/leisure travel demand recovery
stories.summary: Pacific Hospitality Group is opening Denū Hotel & Spa, a 236-room luxury hotel in a newly constructed 17-story building at 1 E. Adams Street in downtown Phoenix, opening September 16, 2026. The hotel features a Hammam-inspired spa, rooftop pool, fitness programs, and flexible meeting and event spaces, positioned near the convention center and entertainment districts. PHG operates 11 properties across the Southwest.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact to multifamily development. However, downtown Phoenix hospitality investment signals confidence in the core's recovery and visitor demand, which can drive ancillary multifamily demand from hospitality workers and service-sector job growth in the urban center—particularly relevant if PHG's expansion correlates with broader corporate/tourism migration to Phoenix.

stories.title: ALDI Reveals Westward Expansion
stories.excerpt: As ALDI enters its 50th year in the United States, the low-price grocer is doubling down on its nationwide expansion, announcing plans to open more than 180 stores by the end of 2026. ALDI is announcing expansion plans into the state of Colorado within the next five years, with more than 50 stores planned for Denver and Colorado Springs. As ALDI continues its westward expansion, the grocer will open 10 new stores in the Phoenix market in 2026 and plans to add a total of 40 new stores by the end of 2030. After debuting four stores in 2025, the grocer will continue to deepen its presence in the growing market with plans to double its current store count by 2030. Additionally, the chain will open two distribution centers in the SW, one in Goodyear, Arizona (projected 2028)and the other in Aurora, Colorado (projected 2029) The post ALDI Reveals Westward Expansion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ALDI announces westward expansion: 180+ stores by end of 2026; 50+ in Denver/Colorado Springs by 2031
Phoenix: 10 new stores in 2026, 40 total by 2030; two distribution centers (Goodyear 2028, Aurora 2029)
Major grocer footprint expansion signals population/household growth and retail-anchored development opportunities
stories.summary: ALDI announced plans to open more than 180 stores by the end of 2026, including expansion into Colorado (50+ stores in Denver and Colorado Springs within five years) and significant growth in the Phoenix market (10 new stores in 2026, 40 by 2030). The grocer will also build two distribution centers: one in Goodyear, Arizona (2028) and one in Aurora, Colorado (2029).
stories.impact: Grocery-anchored mixed-use and suburban multifamily development in Phoenix and Denver metros will see accelerated retail density and neighborhood formation, supporting both renter demand and asset velocity. ALDI's distribution center buildout in Goodyear and Aurora signals inbound logistics job creation, which drives workforce housing demand in those submarkets. This de facto confirms sustained Western population and household formation, validating long-cycle multifamily underwriting in these markets through 2028–2030.

stories.title: Mamdani Sets Sights on Fixing — Not Replacing — Deteriorating Section of BQE
stories.excerpt: Will Mayor Zohran Mamdani be the first administration to finally fix the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) along Brooklyn Heights? Mamdani announced Monday morning that the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) would build bypasses around the surrounding neighborhoods and maintain access to local attractions while finally rebuilding the swiftly deteriorating cantilever portion of the freeway. DOT would build a two-level bypass above Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights, sitting below the promenade and not extending above the current highway. The city would also create a second elevated bypass from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge. The Mamdani administration plans to start the estimated $4 billion project in 2030, despite a sense of urgency from officials. The city estimates the project could take 10 years. The Mamdani administration said it believes this renovation, as opposed to a replacement, will extend the life of the BQE for another 40 years. “After decades of kicking the can down the road and indecision that failed to yield substantial results, we will act with urgency to rehabilitate the city’s portion of the BQE to ensure the safety of New Yorkers and minimize the likelihood of massive traffic diversions into Brooklyn neighborhoods,” DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn said in a statement. “While the city and the state must right the wrongs of Robert Moses with the BQE and other infrastructure plowed through urban communities, decades of political paralysis have left us out of options.” For every year that the city procrastinates, costs increase by an estimated $160 million, according to the announcement. “For decades, prior administrations have failed to deliver urgent long-term repairs to BQE Central — but we can no longer afford to wait for the perfect solution,” Mamdani said in a statement. “We’re going to fix the aging concrete, repair the deteriorating triple cantilever and build temporary roads that keep the highway operabl
bullets: NYC DOT plans $4B repair (not replacement) of Brooklyn-Queens Expressway cantilever; construction starts 2030, 10-year timeline
Proposed two-level bypass above Furman Street; project extends BQE life another 40 years
Long-term infrastructure commitment reduces near-term neighborhood disruption risk for Brooklyn Heights/Nolita multifamily development
stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration announced Monday that the NYC Department of Transportation would repair (rather than replace) the deteriorating cantilever section of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway along Brooklyn Heights. The estimated $4 billion project will build two-level bypasses above Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights and a second elevated bypass to the Manhattan Bridge. Construction is slated to begin in 2030 with a 10-year timeline, extending the BQE's life another 40 years.
stories.impact: This is primarily a transportation/infrastructure story. However, for Brooklyn Heights and DUMBO-adjacent multifamily developers, the 2030 start date and 10-year construction timeline significantly reduce near-term neighborhood disruption risk (noise, air quality, construction traffic) compared to the sword-of-Damocles of accelerated BQE failure. Developers can proceed with moderate confidence in the stability of the Brooklyn waterfront submarket through 2027–2029 lease-ups.

stories.title: Kinsmen Property Group Plans to Bring 322 New Homes to 156-166 Bowery
stories.excerpt: Kinsmen Property Group, a New York City-based real estate development and investment firm, has big plans to build 322 homes along the Bowery in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. After previously filing plans to demolish a 15,000-square-foot set of vacant buildings at 156-166 Bowery in October 2024, Kinsmen has now filed a land use application with the Department of City Planning to transform the now-vacant lot into three mixed-use, mixed-income buildings with a total of 322 homes, according to the firm. If approved, the three buildings would comprise a 29-story building with 124 affordable apartments for seniors; a 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 3,260 square feet of ground-floor retail space; and another 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 4,391 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The project, which would be designed by architects Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, is expected to enter public review through a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) by the end of the year. “We are excited to bring more than 300 new homes to Lower Manhattan at a time when housing is urgently needed across the city,” Ari Zagdanski, principal of Kinsmen, said in a statement. “This project is designed to honor the rich history of the Bowery while also addressing the city’s housing needs head-on.” The site at 156-166 Bowery has already been through various different planned projects. In 2022, previous owner Real Estate Equities Corporation (REEC) — which had signed a 99-year ground lease for the properties in 2020 for $50 million — filed plans to construct a seven-story, 73,000-square-foot retail and office building on the site. Construction on that project eventually stalled. It’s unclear whether REEC still owns the ground lease at the Nolita site, which Kinsmen bought in a set of separate purchases in 2016 and 2017 for a total of $53.5 million, according to records. bullets: Kinsmen Property Group plans 322-unit mixed-use, mixed-income project at 156-166 Bowery (Nolita, Manhattan)
Three buildings: 29-story (124 senior affordable), 26-story + 26-story (99 units each); ground-floor retail; ULURP by year-end
High-density infill development with 40% of units as senior affordable reflects NYC zoning/subsidy alignment
stories.summary: Kinsmen Property Group filed a land use application to develop 322 homes across three mixed-use buildings at 156-166 Bowery in Manhattan's Nolita neighborhood. The project includes a 29-story building with 124 affordable apartments for seniors; two 26-story buildings with 99 mixed-income units each and 3,260 and 4,391 square feet of ground-floor retail, respectively. Designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, the project is expected to enter ULURP (Uniform Land Use Review Procedure) by year-end 2026.
stories.impact: Heavy skew toward senior affordable housing (38% of units) indicates developer reliance on NYC subsidy programs (likely 421-a or similar) to underwrite Nolita's elevated land costs. This signals continued density/entitlement competition in lower Manhattan and reliance on affordable housing mandates to close economics. Market-rate developers should anticipate further affordability requirements and longer entitlement timelines in Manhattan core submarkets.

stories.title: Circle Realty Secures 38K SF of New Leases at 14 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: Circle Realty Group has closed on 37,600 square feet of new leases in Midtown, Commercial Observer has learned. The two largest deals at 225 West 34th Street, also known as 14 Penn Plaza, were for civil engineering company Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 square feet to 14,000 square feet, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which took 14,000 square feet, according to Circle Realty. Bohler signed a 10-year lease and asking rent in the building was $67 per square foot. The length of T&M’s lease was unclear. “These tenants came to me because we’re at the center of transportation and we have a first-class property,” Circle Realty President Jay Futersak told CO. “Tenants know that what we promised is what we deliver.” Futersak represented his own firm in-house and both tenants in the deals. Smaller recent deals in the building were for accounting and advisory firm Calibre CPA Group, which signed a 10-year, 6,100-square-foot lease and is relocating from 462 Seventh Avenue. Mark Furst and Benjamin Saftler of Kaufman Leasing, the brokerage arm of the Kaufman Organization, handled the deal for the Washington, D.C.-based accounting firm and did not immediately comment. Meanwhile, discrimination law firm Fitapelli & Schaffer is also relocating from 20 Liberty Street to 14 Penn with a new 3,514-square-foot lease. Robert Gallucci of Colliers negotiated on behalf of the law firm and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Futersak repped ownership in-house in the Calibre and Fitapelli deals. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Circle Realty closes 37,600 SF office leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 W 34th St) in Midtown Manhattan
Bohler Engineering expanded 8K to 14K SF (10-yr, $67/SF); T&M USA took 14K SF; other smaller tenants
Midtown office leasing resumes despite broader NYC office headwinds; transit-proximate property remains competitive
stories.summary: Circle Realty Group closed 37,600 square feet of new leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 West 34th Street) in Midtown Manhattan. Major tenants included civil engineering firm Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 to 14,000 square feet on a 10-year lease at $67 per square foot, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which leased 14,000 square feet. Smaller tenants included accounting firm Calibre CPA Group.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. However, leasing activity at transit-proximate Midtown office buildings signals selective tenant demand recovery in New York, which supports white-collar job retention and confidence in the Manhattan market. This indirectly validates near-term demand for Midtown-adjacent and East Side multifamily product targeting office workers.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
stories.excerpt: Pluck your average Commercial Observer journalist off the street, shove them in a van, shine a flashlight in their eyes, and say, “Quick — what’s the biggest story in commercial real estate?” nine reporters out of 10 will answer: “Data centers.” At least that’s the case in 2026 after the billions and billions of dollars in investment that have been lavished on the sector. Actually, make that trillion — with a “t.” It’s still a sector that’s largely mysterious and unknown (even the vocabulary of the asset class is new!) so CO was excited last week when San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” which tracks the money behind the $1.3 trillion (and counting) data center bonanza. What makes Atrium’s platform so fascinating is that it delves into the nitty gritty of individual deals like Coreweave’s $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders, and the 24 lenders financing DigitalBridge and IFM’s $20 billion debt facility — but at the same time it examines the breadth of activity of non-bank lenders like PIMCO (which has done $23 billion in originations), or borrowers like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle (five firms that alone account for $223 billion in long-term debt and credit facilities). All this data center activity comes as construction costs have been on the rise. bullets: Atrium launches data platform tracking $1.3T in U.S. data center investments; reveals 38+ lenders in Coreweave's $23B deal
PIMCO, DigitalBridge, Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle dominate origination and borrowing
Non-bank lenders pivoting aggressively to data center debt; capital formation increasingly fragmented and specialized
stories.summary: San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called "Who Finances America's Data Centers" that tracks funding behind the $1.3 trillion data center boom. The platform reveals granular deal-level structures, including Coreweave's $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders and DigitalBridge and IFM's $20 billion facility from 24 lenders, while documenting non-bank lenders like PIMCO ($23 billion in originations) and major borrowers including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Oracle.
stories.impact: Tangential to multifamily but signals massive capital reallocation away from traditional real estate into AI/compute infrastructure. Elevated data center financing costs and non-bank lender specialization may reduce available capital and increase cost of capital for other property types, including multifamily. Developers competing for leverage should monitor data center debt appetite as a leading indicator of broader credit market tightness.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar closes $800M cash acquisition of Zonda; gains access to 3,000+ homebuilders and lot-level development data
Zonda 2025 revenue ~$170M; Zonda addresses $400B annual U.S. new-home sales market
Data consolidation in homebuilding/new construction signals strategic shift toward integrated real estate platforms
stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data and homebuilder software platform. Zonda's lot-level construction and development database serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers and generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. The acquisition gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market.
stories.impact: CoStar's acquisition of Zonda indicates consolidation of real estate data and intelligence platforms. For multifamily developers, this means fewer independent data providers and likely upward pressure on subscription/analytics costs. More significantly, the merger reinforces that data on land availability, entitlements, and pipeline (core inputs to multifamily site selection and competitive positioning) will increasingly reside within vertically integrated platforms controlled by single vendors, reducing developer negotiating leverage on pricing and data access.
